qa.question: Is SPP queue entry GEN-2024-321 the Cross Timbers plant?
qa.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists GEN-2024-321 as a 507 MW gas project in Seminole County, connecting at the Seminole 345 kV substation, with an OG&E owner label and a 2029 in service date. The Cross Timbers permit memorandum at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf describes two turbines of up to 255 MW each at Section 36, Township 6N, Range 5E near Konawa. Two times 255 MW is 510 MW, close to 507 MW.
qa.recommendation: Do not add a new unit for GEN-2024-321 now. Leave the queue entry linked to the Seminole station, and ask the project manager to check the queue study documents to see whether OG&E is buying Cross Timbers output.
qa.note: Nothing I found ties Cross Timbers Power LLC to the queue entry. The queue names OG&E and a substation at the Seminole plant. A web search found no news about Cross Timbers Power. The point of interconnection is the main reason I think it is a different project.

qa.question: Should the Cross Timbers point move about 500 meters?
qa.finding: GEM's point is 34.95195, -96.73905 and is marked exact. The permit memorandum at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf gives 34.95595, -96.73635 for the facility.
qa.recommendation: Leave the point as it is. The two points are about 500 meters apart and GEM's is already exact.
qa.note: I did not open a satellite image. The difference is small compared with the size of the site.
